name: Benaiah
bio:
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was placed over David's bodyguard, the Cherethites and Pelethites, as part of the royal administration David established once his kingdom was secure (2 Samuel 8:18), a position he still held after Sheba's revolt was crushed (2 Samuel 20:23).

Benaiah, a valiant fighter from Kabzeel, is remembered for extraordinary feats of his own: he struck down two of Moab's best warriors, climbed down into a pit to kill a lion on a snowy day, and killed a huge Egyptian warrior armed only with a club, wrestling the Egyptian's own spear from his hand and killing him with it. These exploits won him a name among the Three, David's most elite warriors, though he did not attain to the standing of the top three themselves; David set him over his personal guard (2 Samuel 23:20-23). Benaiah's decisive role in securing Solomon's throne is told in detail in the chapters ahead.
